newsitem.title: LEBANON: Banque Audi shares begin Beirut trading at $15.
newsitem.headline: Banque Audi shares begin Beirut trading at $15.

text.p: Shares in Banque Audi were traded for the first time on the Beirut Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday at $15 a share on turnover of 10,000 shares.
"There were several trades in the Audi shares today," a bourse official told Reuters.

Audi, the second Lebanese commercial bank to list on BSE, offered all its 4,158,000 C shares -- or 30 percent of its total number of shares -- for trading on the market. The bank shares have a nominal value of 2,000 Lebanese pounds ($1.29).
A law passed last year allows Lebanese banks to list and trade 30 percent of their shares on the exchange without prior permission from the central bank.

Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce was the first bank to list its shares on the exchange since it reopened last year after a 13-year shutdown due to Lebanon's civil war. BLC haa been a star performer since they began trading December 30.

At least one other leading Beirut bank, Byblos Bank, is also expected to list its shares soon. Dealers say they expect the bank shares to boost the stock exchange which has been mostly lacklustre since it reopened in January 1996.
